newsitem.title: UK: IPE rules out merger with LIFFE, outlines growth.
newsitem.headline: IPE rules out merger with LIFFE, outlines growth.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on Tuesday outlined several measures to capitalize on deregulation in the energy industry in Europe and ruled out merging with another London exchange.

A one-day strategy meeting of the IPE board and industry officials on December 12 at Nutfield Priory, Redhill, also agreed to set up an Industry Advisory Group to boost trading of its energy contracts.
The IPE will study the feasability of moving the exchange due to limits of its current space, a statement from Richard Reinert, chairman, and Lynton Jones, chief executive, said.
"There was a clear and strong view that in order to achieve the ambitions set out...its members and users would best be served by the exchange maintaining its independence," the IPE said.
"The group thought that this would put an end to speculation about LIFFE 'taking over' the IPE, speculation which has been as unwelcome to LIFFE as it has to the IPE," it said.
LIFFE, the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange, merged with the London Commodity Exchange (LCE) in September.
IPE's plans will be put before the exchange's board in early 1997.
The IPE said it would use its electronic trading system, ETS, for expanding "the global reach of the exchange in after hours trading and...for introducing new contracts."
IPE plans to launch Britain's first natural gas contract on January 31.
The Industry Advisory Group of industry users will give the IPE advice on developments in the energy industry and how that can help the exchange.
A nominating committee will also be set up to ensure that "the various constituencies within the membership of the exchange are properly represented on the board and its committees," the IPE said.
Some changes will be made to the committee structure, it said.
